newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Tutsi rebels blamed for killing of 300 refugees.
newsitem.headline: Tutsi rebels blamed for killing of 300 refugees.

text.p: Marie Nyiratezimana appears to be the only one who survived the killing of more than 300 Hutu refugees by Tutsi rebels in eastern Zaire.
The young woman who escaped what appears to have been a massacre in the Chimanga refugee camp on November 17 hid in a nearby cornfield with heavy injuries to her leg and arm.

"Banyamulenge (Tutsi rebels) came on Sunday and told us all to gather at the camp's central square," Maria said, speaking slowly and sounding distracted, a clear sign of shock and the sufferings she survived.
As she spoke she was trying to comfort her arm, shot through with a bullet, and her leg, parts torn off by shrapnel.

"They told us we have to return home and that they needed to make up list for repatriation," she said on Monday. "But after people gathered on the square they threw something that exploded in the middle of the crowd."
Marie did not know whether it was a hand grenade or a mortar shell. She could not remember anything that followed or how she found herself in the field almost one km (0.7 mile) from the square.

Residents of the nearby village of Kakinda, about 40 km (25 miles) southwest of the provincial capital Bukavu -- now in the hands of the rebels -- said there had been four trucks with up to 40 well-armed rebels who did not try to disguise themselves.
Villagers showed Reuters journalists several sites near the square where the rebels had ordered them to bury the dead. The smell of decomposing bodies was heavy in the air.
The tiny square in front of what appears to have been a community centre carried the signs of the tragedy -- blood-stained clothes, women's and children's slippers.
A little booklet abandoned on the square was open to a page flashing the headline asking in French: "What Prevents People From Living in Peace?"

People from the nearby village said that after the attack, rebels searched the camp -- a compound of clay cabins scattered across the slopes of three hills where once thousands of Hutu families from Rwanda lived -- looking for possible escapees.
The swollen bodies of a young woman and three children could be seen lying on the rubble of their makeshift home in a distant corner of the camp.

"She tried to hide and they (rebels) found her," a village resident who refused to give his name said in a fluent French. "Then they shot her in the leg and left her lying on the ground," said the villager who came across the woman after she was wounded and, when he returned the next day, found her dead.
"When they came the next day she was still alive. And then they finally shot her dead," he said. Empty cartridges were scattered accross the camp.

The rebels, who are fighting against the Zairean government and now control a considerable part of eastern Zaire, appeared in the location of Chimanga earlier this month, prompting an exodus of Hutu refugees from the camp.

More than a half million Hutus from eastern Zaire have crossed back into Rwanda following the rebels' military advance. At least as many are estimated by the U.N. Refugee Agency UNHCR to still be in Zaire.
A group of about 300 Hutu refugees from Burundi had occupied the nearly-abandoned camp just days before the disaster.
The rebels told the residents of Kakinda to keep their mouths shut about the killing and not to help possible survivors or any Hutus.
Some violated the order.
"I come daily to bring Marie some food and just to see her," one young villager said. "After all I am a decent Christian".
But the fear was great and sometimes paralysing.
The village chief disappeared after the shooting leaving junior members of the community to run Kakinda.
Some villagers have been coming every day to destroy what remains of the camp in the hope that if there is nothing left the rebels will not return.
"We witnessed something terrible and they may want to get rid of us," said one villager, setting on fire the straw roof of a cabin. "We want to flatten the whole place. No camp, no reminiscences."
